findings.title: Auth router error middleware answers an unwrapped BodyTooLargeException 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and logs it as a store failure
findings.description: The diff made Core (StandardErrors.statusOf, FinalHandler) and auth's PROD final layer (Auth.prodAnswer) answer an unwrapped BodyTooLargeException 413, but auth's router error middleware (routerError, attached to auth.routes()/adminRoutes(), which apps can extend) still falls through to isStoreFailure, which treats every IOException - now including the public BodyTooLargeException - as a store failure: 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE plus an ERROR line 'auth: a store failed ... answering 503'. So the same exception gives 413 on an app route and 503 + a misleading ERROR log on an auth-router route, while HttpException(413) gives 413 on both. Not a regression (the IOException branch predates the diff), but the diff's classification change is incomplete across the auth layers it chose to touch.
findings.suggested_fix: In Auth.routerError, answer `err instanceof BodyTooLargeException` as respond(req, res, 413, coreCode(413), null, null) before the isStoreFailure branch (or exclude BodyTooLargeException in isStoreFailure and route it to the HttpException-like branch); add a regression test next to AuthClientErrorLoggingTest/JuniorFinalItemsTest asserting 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE and no new ERROR line for an auth.routes() handler throwing new BodyTooLargeException(10), and 500/503 behaviour unchanged for a plain IOException.
